title: Sinner cannot be both remitted and condignly punished
source_text: IV. Sed impossibile erat homini peccatori simul peccatum remitti, & tamen illum pro merito puniri. Cum enim peccatum mortem & perditionem aeternam mereatur, fieri non potuit ut peccator servaretur, fieretque vitae & salutis particeps per divinam misericordiam, & tamen simul poenam peccato condignam subiret.
pass_a_gloss: But it was impossible for the sinful man that sin be remitted and yet he himself be punished according to desert. For since sin merits eternal death and perdition, it could not be that the sinner be saved and made a sharer of life and salvation by divine mercy, and yet at the same time undergo the penalty condign to sin.
pass_b_english: The same sinner cannot both receive remission and undergo sin’s full condign penalty.
Eternal death’s desert bars simultaneous salvation and exacted punishment in him alone.
